ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT obligations are principally governed by Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-1 et seq., including Articles L.561-2, L.561-4-1, L.561-5, L.561-6, L.561-10, L.561-15, L.561-32 and L.561-46 to L.561-50. The beneficial-owner register is governed principally by Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and Articles R.561-55 to R.561-63, as supplemented and amended by Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020, Décret n° 2020-118 of 12 February 2020, and Décret n° 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017. Company registration and filing formalities are submitted through the national guichet unique under Code de commerce, Articles L.123-33 and R.123-1 et seq.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and continuously thereafter, screen all beneficial owners, directors, authorized signatories, major counterparties, banks, and relevant suppliers against United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union restrictive measures, French national sanctions and asset-freeze measures, and OFAC lists where the transaction has a United States nexus. Screen for PEP, family-member, and known-close-associate status under Code monétaire et financier Articles L.561-10 and R.561-18 et seq. Apply enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and enhanced monitoring for PEPs, opaque ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, adverse media, or unexplained payment routes. Retain screening evidence and KYC records for the statutory retention period, generally five years after the end of the business relationship or the relevant transaction, subject to applicable extensions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI: https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name availability and prior-rights searches should also be conducted through the INPI data and trademark databases and the Registre national des entreprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be stated in the articles and registration filings using permitted French characters and must include or clearly correspond to the legal form Société par Actions Simplifiée or SAS. A foreign-language or transliterated commercial name may be used as a trade name or corporate name if it is not misleading, does not infringe prior rights, and is accepted by the registry. The applicant must verify company-name, trade-name, domain-name, trademark, and translation conflicts. A French translation is required for documents submitted in a foreign language unless an accepted exemption applies.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying a regulated public authority, ministry, diplomatic body, or public institution without authorization

Terms implying a bank, credit institution, payment institution, electronic-money institution, insurance undertaking, investment service provider, or financial regulator without the required authorization
Terms implying a medical, pharmaceutical, healthcare, laboratory, or public-health authorization where the proposed activity is not authorized
Terms implying a professional title or regulated profession without the required qualification or registration
Terms likely to mislead the public as to the company's legal form, activity, capital, ownership, or relationship with an existing public or private entity
Names identical or confusingly similar to a registered company, trademark, trade name, domain name, or protected geographical indication
Offensive, discriminatory, unlawful, or contrary-to-public-policy terms

The terms Banque, Assurance, Mutuelle, Crédit, Investissement, Bourse, Hôpital, Université, Ordre, Ministère, République, France, National, Européen, and equivalent protected or sensitive expressions where prior authorization or sector-specific approval is required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not generally provide a universal statutory company-name reservation period of 30 days. The 30-day period is a conservative project-control window for completing incorporation after an availability check and must not be treated as a guaranteed legal reservation. Obtain a written name-availability or prior-rights assessment, submit the incorporation file through the guichet unique, and preserve the filing receipt. If rejected, identify whether the issue concerns legal-form wording, public-order restrictions, regulated terminology, prior rights, or an incomplete filing. Correct the name and resubmit through the guichet unique. For a formal adverse administrative decision, request reasons, file an administrative reconsideration with the issuing authority, and, where appropriate, submit a recours gracieux or recours hiérarchique within two months of notification. A judicial challenge before the competent administrative or commercial court should be assessed with French counsel; an appeal does not automatically suspend the rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office in France and must be able to receive official correspondence and maintain required corporate records. Domiciliation with a specialist commercial domiciliation provider is generally permissible if the provider is authorized under Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-2 et seq. and the domiciliation contract satisfies statutory requirements. A purely virtual office is inadequate where the company performs hospital engineering, medical-gas pipeline installation, equipment storage, project management, technical supervision, employee activity, or regulated operational functions. The registered office does not replace operational premises, technical facilities, professional insurance, safety procedures, or sector-specific qualifications. The medical-gas activity should be mapped against French construction, workplace safety, medical-device, public-procurement, and healthcare-establishment requirements, including applicable standards such as NF EN ISO 7396-1 where relevant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national statistical rate is published for unannounced inspections of newly incorporated SAS entities. For a hospital engineering and medical-gas pipeline business, the practical risk should be assessed as medium: an indicative internal planning assumption is 10% to 25% during the first 24 months for an unannounced or short-notice physical verification by a tax, labor, safety, construction, healthcare, or other competent authority, increasing materially where the company bids for public hospital contracts, employs technical personnel, stores gas-related equipment, reports inconsistent premises, or presents high-risk AML or tax indicators. This is a risk estimate, not an official probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Decree No. 2007-431 on simplified joint stock companies; application of Article 1832 et seq. of the Civil Code on nominal share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) managed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) in the jurisdiction of the registered office; online filing through the INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) Guichet Unique for formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: M0 Incorporation Form (Imprimé M0) together with notarized or certified Articles of Association (Statuts) and evidence of legal publication of the appointment in a journal of legal notices (Annonces Légales).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital requirement for an SAS; shareholders freely set the share capital. The subscribed capital must be fully paid or paid in accordance with the Articles of Association, and if the capital exceeds €300,000 and is in cash, funds may be deposited in escrow with a notary or bank until registration without the need for a blocking certificate; non-cash contributions must be fully paid upon issue.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The first board meeting of the Company was held in Paris. The board unanimously: 1) accepted the subscription of the stated share capital by the initial shareholders and authorized the issuance of shares against cash and intangible contributions; 2) adopted the registered office located at the address recorded in the Articles of Association and approved the complete draft of the Articles; 3) appointed the President identified in the Articles and ratified his power to represent the Company; 4) appointed the Statutory Auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) where legally required; 5) approved the opening of a corporate bank account and authorized the President as sole signatory. Each resolution was adopted without abstention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private notary (notaire) or all shareholders signing by authentic or private deed; later filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder and any co-investors shall amend the model Articles to comply with ISIC 4100 scope. Each shareholder executes the Articles; signatures must be notarized if real estate or a leased asset is contributed. The document must state the corporate name, registered office, capitalization, governing board rules, and authorized corporate purpose limited to installation of medical gas pipelines. A French corporate address and legal representative with EU or French ordinary residence must be designated.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or ID of legal representative
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Articles (e.g., illegal purpose or capital clarity), file a rectified amendment and resubmit the M0 form. An expedited pre-verification may be obtained at the Greffe if a legal representative consults in person.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Stated Capital Account and Obtain Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French registered bank, French branch of an EU credit institution, or Caisse des Dépôts (for cash deposits).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transfer the cash part of the subscribed capital to a non-interest-bearing special account opened for the company formation. The bank issues a capital deposit certificate (Attestation de Dépôt de Capital) listing the shareholders and amounts. If the total capital exceeds €300,000 and is not fully released to the company before registration, the certificate additionally acts as the blocked fund record. Release occurs only after registration certificate is produced.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses due to sanctions list or false identity record, provide a certified IRRER release; select an alternative bank within the same EU banking group and resubmit the authenticity documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Incorporation Notice in a Journal of Legal Notices (Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any authorized journal located in the department of the registered office (approved by the Prefecture).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an announcement (Avis de Constitution) to an approved legal notices journal within the territorial jurisdiction. The notice must include corporate name, legal form (SAS), capital amount, registered office, purpose summary, governance body member names, and the commercial court. The journal renders a copy of the edition containing the notice and an attestation of publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is refused or edited incorrectly, provide a corrected statement to the publisher; publication defective as to purpose must be republished and the eventual registry decision referred to the Greffe for equitable correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Formation Dossier to the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique maintained by the INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 form and upload the signed Articles, capital deposit certificate, legal notice publication proof, and appointment acceptance of the President. Submit the entire dossier digitally. The system assigns a single Business Identification Form (COF), then routes it to the RCS, INSEE, tax and unemployment authorities.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate or notarial certificate
Copy of identity and proof of residence of President
Declaration of non-conviction and good standing for manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS returns a query (e.g., missing capital certificate), correct the dossier in the Guichet Unique within 15 days, pay any differential fee, and obtain a new RCS clearance. Delays may be escalated through the INPI helpdesk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Incorporation Certificate (Extrait Kbis) and Registry Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After verification of the M0 and attached documents, the registry records the SAS and issues an Extrait Kbis (official registration certificate). This certificate serves as legal proof of existence, jurisdiction, and authorized business scope. Lease rights, VAT number, and business insurance can then be activated.
required_dossiers: Extract of the legal notice publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains a clerical error (e.g., address or manager name), request rectification by filing a simpler act before the Greffe clerk, attaching the registration and proof of the error. A fee is charged for certificates beyond the immediate extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Statutory Registrations and Governance Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE (national ID issuance), Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (tax authentication), and Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after Kbis issuance, confirm the assignment of the SIREN/SIRET identification number and the VAT number (SIRET-VAT). Verify the filing of the beneficial owner declaration in the RBE, which must include all shareholders holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights. Adopt and retain a board minute book, statutory meeting ledger, and annual closure calendar in line with the Articles.
required_dossiers: Notice of appointment of statutory auditor if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE declaration is incomplete, the registry will issue a warning; file an amending declaration within 30 days. For sanctuary companies or those with non-EU beneficiaries, consult a French counsel to verify beneficial ownership treatability and possible UBO non-disclosure rulings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) for occupational health and building services; Agence Régionale de Santé (ARS) for technical compliance and quality of installation of medical gases.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat de Conformité Technique des Installations de Fluides Médicaux (Technical Compliance Certificate for Medical Gas Installations) issued after an on-site inspection by a qualified doctor, pharmacist, or engineering firm approved by the ARS; associated operating approval under the Public Health Code (Code de la santé publique, Articles L.5010-1 et seq.).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Régime de déclaration / Enregistrement) under the ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) where waste gases, volatile organic compounds, or hospital wastes are present. Installations above the annual emission threshold require a full EIA, otherwise a simplified environmental note suffices.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Must comply with French Ministerial Order of 2 July 2014 (catalyseur and gaseous effluent thresholds) and European aggressive standards. For copper vacuum and medical oxygen manifolds, no toxic emissions are generated after installation. Wastewater arithmetic mean limits: pH 5.5–8.5, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L; any purge or test gas exhaust must be vented to atmosphere. All solvents and copper etching wastes (if onsite) are collected by licensed waste operators under the ICPE 2790/2795 category.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Requires Fire Safety Certificate (Panneau de Consignation / PC) from the local fire brigade (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours) and a structural load certificate from a certified engineering office demonstrating the floor and ceiling supports for medical gas pipe carriers. A workplace health and safety inspection by the Work Medicine (SST) must certify that the professional installation crews are equipped with oxygen gas certification and pipe test protocols under Labor Code Articles L.4121-1 and R.4222-4.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), French Ministry of Economy and Finance — National portal: impots.gouv.fr; non-resident and foreign enterprise desk: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), 10 rue du Centre, 93108 Montreuil Cedex; centralized corporate registration interface: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique) and infogreffe.fr (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 (domestic SAS): statutory incorporation documents (statuts, acte constitutif, M0) are filed through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, generating the SIREN, SIRET, and NAF/APE Code 4100B registration identity and creating the DGFiP tax file for Impôt sur les Sociétés. Step 2: DGFiP automatically attributes the French VAT registration number (FR + two-digit key + nine-digit SIREN) to taxable persons; where import/export or intra-EU transactions are declared, the operator confirms activation through the impots.gouv.fr professional space (Espace Pro) and elects payment modalities. Step 3 (non-established foreign entity): a foreign contractor performing taxable hospital pipeline installation in France without a permanent establishment must apply directly to the SIEE at Montreuil using the Demande d'Immatriculation TVA (Form V.F.C./4239-FC), appoint a DGFiP-accredited fiscal representative established in France if not EU-established, and wait approximately 4 to 6 weeks for the provisional then final French VAT number; separate RCS registration is required if the foreign entity creates a French PE, while the simplified SAS route remains the standard vehicle for French hospital EPC projects.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Société par Actions Simplifiée is a capital company irrevocably subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, CGI Arts. 206 and 209-I) at 25% standard rate, with no domestic-law pass-through mechanism. Territorial scope: under the French territoriality principle only profits from operations conducted in France enter the IS base; profits of foreign permanent establishments are generally exempt in France unless the parent opts for worldwide taxation. Non-resident shareholders may lawfully hold 100% of the SAS. A 3% surtax (contribution, CGI Art. 235 ter ZCA) is levied on income distributed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: US-style check-the-box classification is not available under French law; the SAS tax classification is fixed. Available elections include: (i) French fiscal integration (Intégration Fiscale, CGI Art. 223 A) permitting a French parent holding at least 95% of a French subsidiary to consolidate taxable results; (ii) option for the worldwide/global territorial regime (Régime Monde, CGI Art. 209 quinquies) with foreign tax credit instead of territorial exemption; (iii) option to form a French VAT group (Assujettis Uniques, CGI Art. 256 C III) permitting the hospital EPC contractor, suppliers, and installation services companies to file a single VAT return; (iv) options under the OSS/IOSS frameworks for B2C supplies; and (v) option for the Group Finance Agreement/Treasury Centralization regime (régime de centralisation de trésorerie). Anti-hybrid rules under EU ATAD apply automatically and offer no elective relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), French transposition of EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC implementing the harmonized European VAT system (CGI Arts. 256 to 298).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France imposes no general economic-turnover registration threshold: any person carrying on a taxable economic activity, including a single occasional supply, must obtain French VAT registration (CGI Art. 286). Small established enterprises may use the optional small-business exemption (Franchise en Base de TVA) up to EUR 85,000 annual turnover for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services (scale applicable in 2025); the SAS medical gas and pipeline installation contractor, executing large hospital contracts, will exceed the franchise thresholds at first contract invoicing and must therefore register immediately with no de minimis allowance. EU-established suppliers may defer French registration for B2C distance sales up to the EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing and transaction data transmission under the 2026-2027 reform (Loi de Finances 2022): from 1 September 2026, large enterprises, and from 1 September 2027, all other taxable persons, must issue B2B invoices in structured format (Factur-X, UBL, CII) and transmit them through either a DGFiP-accredited Plateforme de Démonstration (PDP) or the national Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); B2C transactions require simultaneous automated e-reporting of transaction and payment data to DGFiP. This framework performs validation and digital clearance within five business days of issuance; France does not apply an Italian-style real-time fiscal stamping API, but hospital EPC invoices must carry all mandatory legal mentions (SIREN, VAT number, and contract references) and site-issued cash registers must remain NF 525 anti-fraud certified.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT applies under CGI Art. 262-I-1 where goods are sold and physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union within a period normally ending on the last day of the third month following the month of delivery; the exporter must hold the customs export declaration, transport documents evidencing physical exit of the goods, and commercial documentation identifying the non-EU purchaser. Services ancillary to the exported goods (e.g., on-site commissioning, installation, and terminal manifold connection supplied as part of the exported medical gas system) qualify for the Art. 262-II exemption where the conditions of direct linkage and delivery outside the EU are met. Independent installation and pipeline works performed on immovable property located in France are taxable in France under the Art. 259-A-2° place-of-supply rule and are chargeable at 20% VAT, without export zero-rating; shipments to EU Member States are exempt only as intra-EU supplies under Art. 262 ter with the customer's EU VAT number and Article 289 C recapitulative statement filing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — Déclaration en Douane (DAU) lodged electronically through DELTA/CIE bearing the export MRN and customs exit validation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR International Consignment Note evidencing physical removal of the goods from the European Union
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 foreign-exchange bank credit advice evidencing settlement by the non-resident purchaser
Export Commercial Invoice and underlying purchase order or contract stating Incoterms and ex-France price basis
Commissioning and installation acceptance certificate signed at the foreign hospital site evidencing delivery outside the EU
Intra-EU recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) under Article 289 C CGI verified against the customer's EU VAT number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP verifies export files under the standard three-year limitation period (CGI Art. L.169 LPF), extended to six years for undisclosed activity or ten years for suspected fraud. Where export proof is absent, incomplete, or the goods have not in fact left the EU, the zero-rating is reversed and French VAT is clawed back at 20%; recovery carries 0.20% monthly late interest (CGI Art. 1727), a 40% penalty for deliberate non-declaration (manquement délibéré), 80% for fraudulent maneuvers (manœuvres frauduleuses), and possible additional sanctions under Art. 1732 for fictitious invoicing. Criminal prosecution for VAT fraud (CGI Art. 1741) exposes the managing directors and the appointed French fiscal representative to fines up to EUR 500,000 and up to five years' imprisonment, joint and several liability, and debarment from public hospital tenders; automated data analytics cross-checking customs CIE export movements with VAT returns (Fichier des Écritures Comptables) flags bill-and-switch and circular export schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the Central Bank and statistical agent for balance-of-payments reporting, together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministère de l'Économie as the Foreign Exchange Administration and foreign investment screening authority under the Code monétaire et financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts; intra-EU capital flows are unrestricted under Articles 63 and 64 TFEU, while non-EU flows are liberalised subject to CMF Articles L151-1 to L151-4 and R151-1 to R151-19. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to corporate income tax (IS) compliance, withholding tax on dividends payable to non-resident shareholders under Article 119 ter CGI as reduced by the relevant double tax treaty, and annual financial statement registration; there is no exchange-control blockage. The material caution for this SAS is that the installation of hospital medical gas pipeline networks (oxygen, nitrous oxide, vacuum terminal manifolds) may qualify as an activity essential to the protection of public health within the meaning of Article R151-3 CMF, so a non-EU investor acquiring control must obtain prior authorisation from DG Trésor under the investment-screening regime in force since the decree of 29 December 2023; absent that authorisation, the Banque de France may suspend the inbound capital flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender requirement and no statutory conversion ratio on export receipts. An exporter may lawfully retain export proceeds indefinitely in any convertible foreign currency, repatriate them at its commercial discretion, or convert them on the interbank market through an established credit institution (intermédiaire agréé). The only compulsory obligation is declarative: the depository bank reports each cross-border flow into the Banque de France balance-of-payments system, and the exporting entity must identify the economic motive (trade in goods under NAF 41.00B / 43.21A) and the applicable SWIFT purpose code. Underlying export documentation (customs export declaration, bill of lading, commercial invoice) must be preserved for 5 years to satisfy AML record-keeping and statistical verification requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational EUR Account (compte courant)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with trade finance, documentary letters of credit, and bank guarantee desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and commercial letter of credit channel for hospital EPC imports
Operational Account and Treasury/FX hedging counterpart
Operational Account with public-sector healthcare cash management and cautions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with hard legal caveats. French-licensed or EU-passported electronic money institutions (Qonto, Shine, Revolut Business, Wise Business) can provide multi-currency accounts, payment initiation, FX conversion, and SEPA/SWIFT rails under PSD2 and CMF Articles L525-1 to L525-8, which are adequate for operating cash and supplier disbursements. However, an EMI is not a credit institution: it cannot issue UCP 600 documentary credits, pre-finance trade, issue bid bonds, performance guarantees, cautions or avals required in hospital EPC contracts, act as depositary for an SAS capital increase, or carry full intermédiaire agréé status for Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting. Therefore the SAS must retain a licensed commercial bank as its primary treasury and LC counterpart and use an EMI only as a secondary payments rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is the practical norm: the SAS président holding signature authority must attend the initial client interview before the bank compliance and risk committee, presenting the original or certified K-bis extract, articles of association, corporate resolution of the président, and UBO list. Remote opening by secured videoconference is admitted only for low-risk structures where at least one director is EU-resident and all shareholders are transparent OECD/EU entities; any non-resident or non-EU director will normally be required to attend a second physical interview at the bank branch or a correspondent office. Enhanced KYC under CMF Articles L561-1 to L561-6 and R561-1 additionally requires the business rationale, a 12-month treasury plan, and disclosure of every beneficial owner holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or opaque shareholding chain (non-EU parent with intermediate holding entities)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled full corporate-chain documentation: K-bis extracts and articles of association for each entity, UBO registrations in the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, OECD tax residence certificates, audited financial statements of the parent, certified copies of passports, signed corporate organigram, and proof of authority for the individuals completing the KYC forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk origin or anomalous magnitude of the initial equity injection from a third-country jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blocked-funds certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds) issued by the receiving bank, share subscription agreement, 12-month source-of-funds bank statements of the subscribing entity, verified shareholder loan agreement where the inflow is structured as a current-account advance, SWIFT MT103 remittance chain and beneficiary reconciliation, negative news screening report on all remitters, and a written treasury purpose statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sensitive-sector flag: healthcare infrastructure activity combined with non-EU control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Receipt (récépissé) of the DG Trésor prior-authorisation application where investment screening applies, proof of French operational substance (engineering payroll and hospital contracts), healthcare quality certifications for medical gas pipeline systems (ISO 7396-1, ISO 13485, NF-type documentation), and the hospital tender or purchase award letter evidencing genuine end-use in French medical infrastructure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected rapid cross-border throughput, particularly large EPC prepayments and disbursements within the first 90 days
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 12-month treasury and cash-flow forecast, signed EPC and subcontract agreements listing exact suppliers, pro-forma invoices for copper tubing, oxygen terminal manifolds and vacuum pumps, LC issuance plan, third-party commercial rationale memorandum, and written acceptance of ongoing transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status or sanction-list proximity of shareholders, officers, or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP disclosure declaration (interposition de personne politiquement exposée), complete beneficial ownership attestation, evidence of legitimate professional income and wealth (tax returns, salary certificates, share-purchase instruments), reference from a recognised credit institution, and written acceptance of reinforced monitoring (compte soumis à surveillance renforcée).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Stepwise compliant route: (1) if the subscribing shareholder is non-EU and the SAS performs sensitive healthcare-listed activities, obtain DG Trésor prior authorisation before transferring any funds; (2) the subscribing shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 credit transfer quoting purpose code CAPC (capital contribution), the SAS SIREN/SIRET, and the dedicated blocked-account reference; (3) the French receiving bank credits the funds to the capital blockage account and issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds, enabling the président to file the capital increase with the commercial court registry; (4) after registry registration and tax formalities, the funds are released to the operational EUR account; (5) the bank and the SAS record the flow as direct investment, cash capital contribution, in the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting and retain the UETR, SWIFT confirmations, blocked-funds certificate, and share subscription deed indefinitely. Outbound dividend or shareholder-loan repayment flows reverse the same labelling using the corresponding direct investment or intercompany loan purpose codes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail for hospital EPC imports (copper tubing, pressure regulators, oxygen manifolds, vacuum pumps): irrevocable documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 issued by the French bank via SWIFT MT700 and discharged by MT400 or MT202 COVER settlement upon compliant presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and medical gas equipment conformity certificates. Open-account settlements on the SWIFT gpi network via MT103 with purpose code TRAD and full invoice and bill-of-lading references are acceptable for low-value consumables. Domestic subcontractor payments run over SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant; receipts from public hospitals or healthcare authorities arrive as wires into the operational account quoted on the K-bis; the treasury should automatically convert surplus FX balances into EUR at booking to avoid unhedged residual exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (change à terme ferme) for EUR/USD and EUR/CNH with tenors matched to EPC project milestones
FX swaps (swap de change) for temporary cross-currency liquidity bridging between EUR and USD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on non-convertible or restricted currencies, where offered by an authorised French credit institution for offshore CNH/USD hedging
Vanilla FX options (call and put) and risk reversals documented under an FBF/ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) aligned to long-term shareholder loan or project financing maturities
Monthly automatic FX conversion sweeps under a pre-approved treasury credit line with audited exposure limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court-authorized extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court injunction, daily penalty payment, and management liability; no fixed automatic strike-off deadline solely for failure to approve accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and applicable management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months after approval for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Legal representative may incur a EUR 1,500 fine, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; registry injunction and subsequent administrative dissolution or strike-off procedures may apply, with no uniform automatic strike-off period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end, through electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge generally 10% of tax due, increased interest generally 0.20% per month, and possible tax audit or enforcement action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual confirmation is required; filing is required upon incorporation and promptly after any change in beneficial ownership or control information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update may result in formal notice, judicial measures, monetary penalties, and restrictions on registry compliance; no annual filing deadline applies where no change occurs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered office and corporate particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry and INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual confirmation filing; changes to registered office, officers, articles, or other registered particulars must be filed within the applicable statutory period after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted change filings may trigger registry rejection, fines, injunctions, and potential administrative dissolution or strike-off procedures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for a SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the end of two consecutive financial years: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Additional appointment obligations may apply to parent companies, controlled entities, or qualifying groups.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations; IFRS may apply in specified consolidated-accounting contexts but is not the default framework for standalone SAS statutory accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual beneficial-owner confirmation where no information has changed. The SAS must update the beneficial-owner filing after any change in ownership, voting rights, control, or identification data and maintain evidence supporting the ownership chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or shareholder accounts
Register of share transfers and movements
Register of decisions of the shareholders or sole shareholder
Minutes and written decisions of corporate bodies
Beneficial-owner records and supporting ownership documentation
Accounting books and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 600-1,800 per year for a standard registered-office or domiciliation service; higher for mail handling, premises access, or regulated administrative support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,500-12,000 for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; approximately 12,000-35,000 for a larger or group-connected entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% standard rate; SME reduced rate of 15% on first €42,500 turnover; R&D tax credit up to 30% of qualifying expenses; innovation status benefits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200 or electronic Déclaration de résultat via impots.gouv.fr portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 April for calendar year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover excluding VAT for the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-sourced turnover; non-residents must declare French branch or PE income
For non-residents, include French permanent establishment profits; losses may be carried forward

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.5% of tax due per month of delay, minimum €50; up to 5% maximum; criminal penalties for willful non-filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Treaty Relief Certificate) or equivalent documentation to French tax authorities via impots.gouv.fr; obtain confirmation of reduced rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory, reduced to 0-10% under most treaties; Interest: 25% statutory, reduced to 0-10% under treaties (e.g. 0% under EU directives)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million group turnover for Local File; €750 million for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France implements ESR; entities must demonstrate adequate economic substance for activities like holding or IP management; non-compliance triggers recharacterization and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty: up to 5 years imprisonment and €500,000 fine; civil penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, fines, and imprisonment if complicit

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a shell entity without genuine business operations or economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions; denial of deductions; penalties up to 500% of tax evaded
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors liable for restitution and potential imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering reporting or KYC requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 5% of turnover; criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and potential disqualification from office
